claim: Where a street ends at the map's edge it must look as if the town goes on: the buildings beside the mouth carry on past the boundary wall at the same height and front, lower roofs behind them, and a barred gate through which the paving and lamps continue -- never a plain wall cut off by sky. Blood does it with an unreachable court whose walls wear other buildings' tiles and a sector of no height where the sky comes down.
evidence: the owner, 2026-11-25: 'These walls on the city borders should have hint of continuing behind even it is unreachable'; and 'think about it like continuation of the buildings you see next to it'
use: Build each end as an arrangement beyond the edge; raise floors of whole storeys for what stands behind, never lower the sky.
